turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hi there, I was just hoping to ask you a few questions today but I was wondering if you could tell me what brought you in today.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am just calling about my daughter. She's been sick over the last few days. She has fever and a cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK. When did the fever and cough start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So they started around three to four days ago. And around the same time she was also having like a runny nose.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and has the fever and cough been present the whole time?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah I would say they started around the same time and ah, they have been going on for the last three and a half to four days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so has there been a period when she hasn't had a fever or a cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, every time I've measured it, she has had a fever and she's been coughing for the last few days. Hasn't really changed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, can you think of anything leading up to these symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, she was she was fine, just three to four days ago. Like before that she was her playful self. No issues. But yeah, it's for the last couple of days just this nonstop cough and the fevers is what's really worrying me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uh, have the symptoms have gotten worse or stayed the same?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say the fever has been getting a little bit worse over the last like, especially today, but the cough, coughing is about the same as what it was when it first started three days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Has she been sick like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: She's, she often gets sick, like her brother goes to daycare and he brings a lot of bugs from there and every time he gets sick, she also gets sick. The last time she had like a similar cough was around two months ago, but at that time I wasn't that worried because she didn't have any fevers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, have you, has there been anything that you've tried to help with the cough or fever?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh Tylenol, I gave her Tylenol. It did help her a little bit, but then the fever came right back, uhm say like a few hours later.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and anything you notice that's made the cough or fever worse over the last three or four days?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not anything that I know of. Her fevers been getting worse, but I don't really know why that is.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uh, has she been having any other symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, other than like, yeah, she had that runny nose when it first started, and then she's also been having some diarrhea.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when did the diarrhea start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think I would say it started around two days ago. She's, like every time I change her diaper she would have like 4-5 different diaper changes throughout the day, and they they seem pretty liquid. So I think yeah, she's been having diarrhea for the last two days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uh you mentioned liquid appearing stool, what would you say say, so I guess, could you comment on the consistency and colour?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Consistency, I'd say it's pretty watery, like diarrhea and colour I didn't really think there's any changes in in the colour.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So you didn't think there was any blood in the stool?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, no, I didn't see any blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, as for the fever, what was the maximum temperature that you noted and how did you check it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I used, we have just a regular non digital thermometer in her ear and her temperature today was around 103 degrees Fahrenheit.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, did you notice any tugging or pulling at her ear?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, she doesn't seem to have any irritation there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uh, how about any vomiting or regurgitation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, she's been keeping food down. No issues there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and notice any discharge from either eye?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about any discharge from ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not that I've noticed, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Notice any rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I didn't not know like new rashes, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and how is she been in terms of mood or or behaviour?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh she's been pretty like she's not herself over the last few days. She's been crying a lot more, just very irritable.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, would you say inconsolable at times?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sometimes like yesterday like she, I couldn't get her to stop crying.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and uh, I know you said no vomiting, but has she been coughing up any sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I would say, uh, this green slimy content. Yeah, it's like green and slimy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, how much would you say, uhm, like a cup, or more?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say probably like at least, at least a couple spoonfuls at a time, she would cough up.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you notice any blood in it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I didn't notice any blood at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and with the cough, have you noticed any difficulties breathing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I don't know if it's difficulty breathing, but I have noticed sometimes she's like breathing faster than normal, like taking a lot more breaths.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK. Uh, is she having troubles with drooling or your trouble speaking?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no. I haven't noticed that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does her voice sound normal to you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think her note, her voice hasn't really changed that much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, with the noticing the faster rate of breathing is the breathing noisy at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, like she's not wheezing or anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you notice any like retraction of the skin between her ribs when breathing.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh so like, uhm, like what do you mean by that?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Like just so when she's breathing in and out. Is she generating a lot of force and effort to really kind of suck in and blow out so you can kind of see impressions over the ribs.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, I I don't think I've noticed that, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, and, have you noticed any blueish discolouration around her lips or mouth?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any urinary problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, she's peeing fine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how has she been sleeping the last few days?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: She hasn't really been sleeping in between the crying and like just being so irritable. I think she's just very uncomfortable when she's trying to get to sleep, so I would say not, like maybe a couple hours for the last few nights.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any evidence of seizure or limb jerking?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, not that I've noticed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. And and have you notice an her being like really lethargic at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, she's not herself and she's still like pretty active, like she's, she just seems really unhappy and irritated. But no, she still has energy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And uh, is she drinking yeah, a lot more fluids or or a lot less? How is she tolerating oral intake?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say I think she's more on the dryer side like she, her mouth is very dry. Her lips are like all cracked, and she it seems that she's drinking less water too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK. And, uh, how many wet diapers would you say in the last 24 hours?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um? Yeah, it's difficult to say. I think I like yesterday changed four to five times. They were all diarrhea, so not really sure, but maybe around 5.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you guys traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No. No, we've been here.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so next just some questions about past medical history. Uh, has she had any medical problems in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The only thing I could think of was after she was born, she had to be given the light treatment for like jaundice, but after that no other problems.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any prior surgeries?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any previous hospitalizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just the light treatment, but other than that nothing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and throughout pregnancy were there any complications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, my pregnancy was completely normal. No complications during the pregnancy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so no gestational diabetes or hypertension?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and uh, were you sick at all at any point with infectious symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, everything came back clear. All the tests were normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um. Any allergies to medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No allergies.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is she currently taking any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just tried the Tylenol but it didn't really seem to work.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and has she been around anybody sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just her big brother who goes to daycare was also like a bit sick with a cough and some runny nose for the last four days. But, uhm, he didn't have a fever and he seemed to recover pretty fast but seems she may have caught it from him.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and anybody in the family um, have any similar symptoms right now? I guess besides her brother?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just just her and her brother.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, and in regards to birth, birth history, was it a vaginal delivery or C-section?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was a normal vaginal delivery at 38 weeks there were no problems after the delivery or before the delivery.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and uh are her immunizations up to date?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah uh, all our immunizations are up to date.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um, in regards to growth and development, have you had any concerns?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, we've been getting her checked regularly. It seems that she's been growing well and developing well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and who is the primary caregiver for at home?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Primary caregiver, right now I'm staying home with her and her brother goes to daycare. So yeah, it would be me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, and could you tell me about her eating habits and typical appetite?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, so now like she is able to eat like everything like vegetables, fruits, breads and meat, but over the last few days she has been just irritable with everything. So even eating food has just not been great for the last few days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when was her last checkup?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So it was around one month ago and everything was fine then. No concerns from the doctor.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Thank you.
